steps.text: Gather the ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Mix ground beef, eggs, bread crumbs, and ketchup in a large bowl until well combined. Season with Italian-style seasoning, oregano, basil, garlic salt, diced tomatoes, and cheese. Press into a 9x5-inch loaf pan, and cover loosely with foil.
Bake in the preheated oven until internal temperature reaches 160 degrees F (70 degrees C), about 1 hour.

raw_recipe.headline: Best Italian Meatloaf
raw_recipe.description: Italian meatloaf made with ground beef, Italian-style seasoning, basil, tomatoes, and mozzarella cheese is a delicious twist on regular meatloaf.

video.description: Take a vacation away from the land of regular meatloaf to the excitement of Europe with Italian herbs and spices. All the hominess of meatloaf is dressed up with tomatoes, cheese and Italian-inspired herbs for a loaf that’s perfectly moist and exceptionally flavorful and begging to be displayed on a bed of mashed potatoes.
video.name: Italian Meatloaf I

Bake in the preheated oven until internal temperature reaches 160 degrees F (70 degrees C), about 1 hour.

review.reviewBody: This is a phenomenal recipe--one of my favorites so far from this site. I did tweak it just a little. I used a little over 2 lbs of lean ground beef cause that's what I had. I used 1 cup of italian seasoned bread crumbs and 1/2 cup of sphagetti sauce instead of the ketchup. I also used the diced tomatoes with garlic and onion. This made 2 meat loaves for me. The texture was perfect; moist but held together well and the flavor was amazing. I served it with bowtie pasta tossed with parmesan and the rest of the jar of spaghetti sauce, garlic bread and steamed veggies. This was an easy and delicious meal that my family loved! Thanks for the great recipe.

Insta Pot Friendly! I was using my oven for Eggplant Parmesan II (also on this site) so I did this meatloaf in my InstaPot. With a trivet and 3/4 C water in the pot, put pressure setting on high for 25 min, allow 10 min for pre-heat, release steam after 10 min; total 45 min. I covered my steamer basket with foil on the outside, patted the loaf into it, placed it in a silicone sling made for InstaPot, and lowered all into the pot. The flavors are mild and definitely Italian...you can play with them as desired.

I would put this at 3 1/2. It was not what I expected. I expected it to taste like a big meatball, but it was drier than that. I thought there would be too much chunky tomato, but there wasn't. The mozzarella completely vanished. I did use less of the herbs - 3/4 tsp instead of a full tsp for all, and I'm happy I did that. Overall, it tasted good, but I found it dry. I would definitely put some sort of marinara sauce over the top. It really needs it. And I would probably put the full 2 cups of mozz into it (an 8 oz bag) as well as some parmesan. I never cook meatloaf in a loaf pan, always free form so that it's not swimming in grease, and I'm happy I did that. My husband loved it, I thought it was ok, I'll tweak it next time to make it better.

Easy to make and great tasting! I did use a blend of 1 lb ground beef and 1 lb sweet Italian sausage, though, also used another tip from below and used spaghetti sauce instead of ketchup - since I topped with more spaghetti sauce (hubby likes his sauce!) I find if I mix my dry spices/herbs in a small bowl and crush with my fingers before adding, they release a lot more flavor!

I've been looking for something other than the traditional meatloaf and decided to try this one. My husband absolutely despises ketchup so I substituted chunky spaghetti sauce as another review suggested. I do not have a meatloaf pan so I formed a larger loaf (about 10 x 6 x 2) and baked it on a foil lined jelly roll pan. It turned out moist and delicious. Husband ate a second helping and said a couple of times that it was really good. Served it with angel hair pasta with butter and parmesan along with a bakery garlic loaf. This will be a keeper for us.

After reading reviews, I did adjust the amount of liquid - so used one egg, 10 ounces of diced tomatoes and I mixed 1 cup of cheese into the meat mixture (the rest, I added to the top of the meat loaf with about 15 minutes left in the cooking). The result was very moist and tasty. I used panko crumbs and 3 cloves of fresh garlic for the garlic salt (so did add some salt and pepper before putting the meat loaf in the oven). I baked it in a 375 degree oven, without the foil (I used the foil to line the pan) and it cooked in 45 minutes (just the thing for a quicker meal). Delicious and a great change from other meat loaf recipes I have tried. Thanks for the recipe Stefanie.

I always make this version. Very yummy. Generally adjust ingredient amounts accordingly because I use only 1lb of ground beef. Add a little parmesan to the top also. I have added diced up zucchini to the mix (just because why not). I have made it muffin cups for individual servings...cooks quicker. Definitely a keeper!

This was delicious! My tweaks: 1. Used fired roasted diced tomatoes 2. Mix Italian/moz cheese 3. Added 1/2 cup milk 4. Added 1/4 cup chopped onion 5. No garlic salt. Salt and garlic powder combo 6. Topping: ketchup, touch of brown sugar, dash garlic powder and of Lewrys season salt (put on top when temp hit 160). Returned to oven and broiled a few min to finish off and thicken up sauce. 7. I did drain meatloaf 3/4 way through 1 hr cook time. Cook time closer to 1 hr, 20m

Oh my gosh so good. I used 1.27 pounds of ground chuck. Really really drained the diced tomatoes and reduced basil and oregano to 1/2 tsp. Only put 1 cup of mozzarella in the meat loaf and topped it with the other 1/2 cup for the last 10 minutes. Instead of ketchup, I used pizza sauce. THIS IS A KEEPER!

You know me. I'm the woman whose meatloaf used to clear a room! The announcement of "Tonight's meatloaf night" always elicited the response of, "I have plans tonight." "I'm eating at my friends house!" "Meatloaf! AGAIN!"
Tonight I made THIS meatloaf and they were begging me for more! "When are we having this again?" "Tomorrow?" 
This was absolutely the best meatloaf I've ever tasted! I also used spaghetti sauce instead of ketchup, Italian breadcrumbs and instead of garlic salt, I used minced garlic. I also didn't use the basil, or oregano since I used diced tomatoes with garlic, basil and oregano and my spaghetti sauce had garlic and onions in it. I did, however use the Italian seasoning and that was perfect!
I also added Parmesan cheese, baked it for 1 hr and 20 minutes and the last 20 minutes of cooking time, I removed the foil and sprinkled some leftover moz cheese on the top. SUPREMO!!! And it didn't need onions, BTW. Just fine, moist and tasty without them.
Thanks for this recipe! It's definately replacing to old, dry boring one I used to use!
I'm adding this little addendum after reading a recipe here for onion encrusted meatloaf and decided I'm going to try the Italian Meatloaf I and just top with french fried onions. I think they just made Heaven BETTER!!!

Being diabetic I stay away from the brown sugar. Recipe didn't say what to do with the mozzarella so I just sprinkled it on top and only needed 1/3 the amount. Used Italian meat loaf meats from my Italian store which is a mix of 1/3 each; ground beef, veal & pork. Then I used fresh peeled tomatoes & added fresh garlic, onions, green peppers & fresh basil to the other ingredients. Easy to make but needed a 9x6 loaf pan (which I have). Invited mom over...just fab!
I used 2 Cups mozzarella, otherwise followed exactly. Served over buttered egg noodles - no sauce needed!
Comes out greasy Although the recipe was followed the seasoning over power the dish
My husband and son 💙 this recipe
We used venison instead of beef and also added sautéed onions
Added 2 extra tsp of Italian seasoning because I didn’t have the dried oregano or dried basil and used regular salt and 1/2 diced onion 4 cloves minced garlic instead of garlic salt.

Very good! I only used 2 lb of ground beef and kept the recipe as is, except I added a little more of everything, replaced the ketchup with marinara sauce and omitted the diced tomatoes. I also added 2 TB of parmesan cheese and 2 tsp of Worcestershire sauce. I removed the foil for the last 10 minutes. My family liked it, but complained that you couldn't taste the mozzarella. So, the next time I did it, I kept the mozzarella in the beef mix, but then I put a layer of mozzarella in the center. I also added marinara sauce after it was done. It was delicious!
This was an awesome recipe. Very moist, just the right amount of seasonings. Instead of using mozzarella I used the Italian 6 cheese blend. Will definitely make this over and over again.
Used diced cheese instead of shredded. Needed more Italian seasoning. 🧂

I've been making this for ever. I NEVER use ketchup. Always use classico. 1.5 cups Mozzarella mixed in. In glass pan cover with MORE sauce, top with 1.5 each shreaded Parmesan and Mozzarella. Bastered out most of the grease. Round 2 later.
